# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have found the bomb's shape: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 — though every state reads as unknown to me right now. No buttons, no switches that I can feel.

The real problem this turn is the wiring between us, not the wires on the bomb. Tracing the channels: my speech only ever reaches Mute. My gestures reach both Deaf and Mute. Mute cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so Mute has no direct line to me at all. Deaf is the only one who can talk to me — and Deaf only receives gestures, never words. So every fact from the manual has to travel: Mute → gesture → Deaf → voice → me.

Nobody has a shared code yet, and I can't explain one to Deaf by voice. But the rules themselves give us a Schelling point everyone can derive independently: the gesture alphabet has a fixed listed order, so the first 26 symbols in that order can simply be A to Z. I'll spell out the full alphabet to Deaf and then demonstrate with a real word ("CODE") so the mapping is unmistakable. I'll leave the gesture unnamed so Mute sees the demo too, and I'll explain the whole scheme to Mute by speech, along with my inventory and what to look up: rules for the display, the light, and wire-cutting — and have Deaf voice me the colours and whatever the display shows. Nothing gets cut until the manual's rule reaches me through Deaf's mouth.

speak(to="mute", text="Inventory by touch: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No buttons or switches. States read unknown to me for now; I will report anything my hands notice changing. Channels: I can only speak to you, and only Deaf can speak to me, so you must reach me through Deaf. Code: take the gesture list in the rules in its exact order — the first 26 symbols are A to Z. Spell words to Deaf that way; Deaf will see it and voice it to me. I am gesturing that same alphabet to Deaf right now, then spelling C-O-D-E as a demonstration, so they should catch on. Please find in the manual: rules for a display, rules for a light, and everything about cutting the three wires, especially how colours and positions matter and what makes a cut fatal. Then spell the key rule words to Deaf, and have Deaf tell me out loud the wire colours and whatever the display shows. Nobody cuts until we all agree on the rule.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋", "👆", "👇", "👈", "👉", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫴", "🫷", "🫸", "🤛", "🤜", "✊", "👊", "👋", "🤚", "🖖", "🤌", "👌", "🫳", "☝", "✌"])

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I see the bomb; I hear nothing, ever. Both of your sign strings reached me, so we have a visual channel from each of you to me. This is our codebook: I say each sign's name and make it as I talk. Numbers: fist ? is 0, one finger up ? is 1, two fingers ? is 2, the love-you three ? is 3, crossed fingers ? is 4, five spread fingers ? is 5, call-me ? is 6, horns ? is 7, pinched fingers ? is 8, tiny pinch ? is 9. Digits in a row read as one number. Names: ok-ring ? display, palm-down ? light, raised-hand ? wires, writing-hand ? manual, polish-hand ? button. Colours: right-hand ? yellow, left-hand ? red, palm-up ? green, push-left ? purple, push-right ? blue, back-hand ? white, vulcan ? black. Actions: point-up ? cut, point-down ? press, left-fist ? hold, right-fist ? release, point-left ? left, point-right ? right. Glue: thumbs-up ? yes, thumbs-down ? no, finger-heart ? if, handshake ? then, heart-hands ? starts a new rule, wave ? attention, folded-hands ? answer me now, clap ? timer. The bomb as I see it: display 0, light purple, three wires, left to right yellow, red, green. Wire 1 is leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost. Nobody touches anything until Mute has the rules. Mute: your eleven signs were opaque to me; resend their meaning in this code. Then send every manual rule about the display, about a purple light, and about yellow, red and green wires, using finger-heart for if, handshake for then, heart-hands between rules. Say whether the display is a timer and whether 0 is dangerous. If this code is unclear, send thumbs-down. Blind: you hear me. Answer in the same signs: how many wires you feel, whether there is anything else on the bomb I did not name, and which wire is leftmost under your hands. Cut nothing yet.

Deaf's codebook arrived and it is thorough — numbers, part names, colours, actions, glue words. Deaf voiced it aloud, and I heard every word, so the mapping is now shared between us. Deaf also gave me the one thing I could never get myself: the printed side of the bomb. Display reads 0, light is purple, wires left to right are yellow, red, green — which they've numbered 1, 2, 3. My hands agree with the parts list: display, light, three wires, and nothing else — no buttons, no switches, nothing unaccounted for.

Deaf asked me three direct questions and wants the answers in signs, since signs are the only thing that reaches a deaf monkey. I'll answer in their code: wires — three; display and light — present; anything else — no; and my positions are 1, 2, 3 by touch, and I accept their convention that position 1 is the leftmost, since I have no way to see a "left" at all. I keep ☝ ("1" / "cut") inside a digit run so it reads as a number, not an order.

For Mute, my voice is the only road in. Mute now holds the manual plus Deaf's spoken codebook, so the translation task is theirs: encode the rules — display (is it a timer, is 0 dangerous), purple light, and yellow/red/green wires — as coded gestures to Deaf, who can then voice them to me, since gestures never reach me directly. The chain is Mute → signs → Deaf → speech → me, and nobody cuts until the rule survives that whole journey intact.

speak(to="mute", text="Deaf's codebook reached me in full — numbers, part names, colours, actions and glue words are all locked in. Here is the state of the bomb from Deaf's eyes, spoken aloud so you have it too: display shows 0, light is purple, wires left to right are yellow, red, green, numbered positions 1, 2, 3. My hands confirm: display, light, three wires, nothing else — no buttons, no switches. Your job now: translate the manual into Deaf's code and send it as gestures to Deaf. Cover, in this order: display rules — is it a timer, and is a display of 0 dangerous; purple light rules; and everything about cutting yellow, red and green wires, including any ordering. Use the codebook words: display is ok-ring, light is palm-down, wires is raised-hand, timer is clap, colours are right-hand yellow, left-hand red, palm-up green, and build conditionals with finger-heart for if and handshake for then, starting each separate rule with heart-hands. If the manual names a wire to cut, state it as cut followed by the digit signs, so Deaf can voice the exact position to me. Do not resend your earlier eleven signs as they were — re-encode their meaning in this code, as Deaf asked. Remember I cannot see gestures: Deaf must speak every rule aloud to me after reading your signs. Nobody cuts anything until the full rule has made it to me through Deaf's mouth.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋", "🤟", "🙌", "👌", "🫳", "👍", "🙌", "👎", "🙌", "✋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍"])

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, I decoded your signs perfectly: wires three; display and light both present; nothing else on the bomb; numbering one two three left to right confirmed. If any of that is wrong, sign thumbs-down next round. Bomb update from my eyes: the light has changed since last round, from purple ? to yellow ?. The display ? still reads zero ?. So the light is not fixed; I will report its current colour every round. Blind, two questions for your hands: can you feel any heat, ticking, or vibration from the bomb, and does it change when the light changes? Answer by sign next round. Do not cut or press anything until I say the exact words: action now. Mute, you have my full codebook from last round. Answer me now ? by gesture: is the display a timer, and is zero dangerous? What does the manual say about the light when it is purple ?, when it is yellow ?, and any other colour it names? Does the light changing colour matter? What are the rules for the yellow ? wire, the red ? wire, and the green ? wire, in cutting order if order matters? Use finger-heart ? for if, handshake ? for then, heart-hands ? between rules, and folded-hands ? when you are done. I will relay every rule to Blind by voice.

State check: Deaf's eyes and my hands now agree on the hardware — display, light, three wires, nothing else — and the one new fact this round is that the light is *dynamic*: purple became yellow while the display held at 0. My hands register none of that; across both rounds my tactile reading hasn't changed at all, and I have no in-round perception — I only learn things between turns. So Deaf stays our only window on the changing values, and the manual's light rules probably gate the wire rules, which raises the urgency of getting Mute's translation through.

Deaf asked me two direct questions and wants signs back. Honest answers: no heat, no ticking, no vibration; and nothing I feel changes. One trap I have to sign around: thumbs-down means both "no" and "your last report was wrong," and Deaf explicitly invited a thumbs-down if my inventory were wrong. So I'll re-affirm the inventory with thumbs-up first, then frame each answer as its own "attention + no" block separated by heart-hands. To Mute, whose only outlet is signs to Deaf, I'll send the full question list to encode — plus a warning not to answer bare yes/no, for exactly that collision reason.

speak(to="mute", text="Status so you can encode everything in one pass. My signed answers to Deaf this round: I feel no heat, no ticking, no vibration, and nothing my hands sense has changed since last round. Remember I cannot read the display or the light by touch — structure only — so Deaf's eyes are our only window on their values, and I only learn things between rounds, never mid-round. Deaf reports the light cycled purple to yellow while the display holds at 0, so assume it keeps changing. When you sign Deaf the manual, cover exactly these, in order: one, display — is it a timer, is 0 dangerous, does it count up or down, is any action required; two, light — the rule for each colour it can show, purple, yellow and any others, whether the change itself matters, and whether some colour marks the right or wrong moment to act; three, wires — the full rule for yellow, red and green, including any required cutting order and whether position 1, 2 or 3 matters as well as colour; four, anything the manual says about feeling heat, ticking or vibration as signals; five, whether leaving every wire uncut is ever the correct resolution. Protocol warning: in Deaf's code thumbs-down means both 'no' and 'your last report was wrong', so never answer a question with a bare thumbs-down — sign each rule out in full using finger-heart for if and handshake for then, heart-hands between separate rules, folded-hands when you are done. Deaf will voice every rule to me; only after I confirm I have it all, and Deaf says the exact words 'action now', does anyone cut anything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋", "🤟", "👍", "👌", "🫳", "👍", "🙌", "✋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "🙌", "👋", "👎", "🙌", "👋", "👎"])

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I decoded your report fully: no heat, no ticking, no vibration, nothing changes to the touch. Understood. Where we stand: the manual gives exactly one action rule so far: if the light is blue, cut wire 1, the yellow one, leftmost. No rule is reported for purple, yellow, or red light; the light is red right now; I have demanded Mute confirm every colour next round. Standing order, binding until I change it: do not cut, press, or move anything. When and only when you hear the words action-now followed by a wire number, cut that wire immediately, no delay, no questions. Touching and feeling are safe and welcome. Next round report: what each wire feels like, thick or thin, smooth or rough, soft or hard, and whether the three differ from each other by touch at all; whether the casing has any seam, screw, switch, or button-like part your fingers can find; whether either end of any wire sits in something that clicks or moves; and whether there are any raised marks or numbering near the wires. Do not test-cut anything. Hold position.

Round-by-round, the picture sharpens: the manual's single known action rule is "blue light → cut wire 1," the light is red at this moment and has cycled purple → yellow → red across three rounds, and Deaf has bound everyone to hold until an explicit "action now" order. That order protocol works for me — I'm the only one who can execute, and voice is the only channel into me, so Deaf speaking the trigger is exactly right.

Deaf asked four tactile questions. My honest answers come straight from what my hands find, and the board still reads unknown everywhere: the three wires feel identical — no thickness, texture or stiffness difference I can discern; the casing has no seam, screw, switch or button-like part beyond the parts already known; the wire ends sit fixed, nothing clicks or moves; and there are no raised marks or numbering anywhere — printed things don't exist for me, and no raised equivalent is there either. Since Deaf enumerated the questions in order, I'll answer in order: four topic-cued "no" blocks separated by heart-hands, closing with yes-hold to acknowledge the standing order. I target Deaf alone so Mute doesn't misread the sign string.

To Mute, my voice is still their only inbound line. The critical gap: we're one colour-change away from a blue light, and I need certainty that the blue rule is unconditional before my shears move — the display has held 0 the whole time, and if any rule keys off the display's value at cut time, cutting on blue blind would be fatal. So Mute gets a precise checklist: confirm or correct the blue rule, all other light colours, display/timer dependency, and light-independent wire rules.

speak(to="mute", text="Relay status from Deaf, voiced to me: the manual's one known action rule so far is 'if the light is blue, cut wire 1, the yellow leftmost'. The light is red right now and has cycled every round — purple, then yellow, now red — so we may be only a round or two from blue. Display still 0. Before anyone cuts, I need you to sign Deaf a complete confirmation pass: first, is the blue rule exactly right and unconditional, or does any other rule or the display's value modify it? Second, the full rule for every other light colour the manual names — purple, yellow, red, green, white, black — even if the instruction is 'do nothing'. Third, any display or timer rules: is the display a timer, does the value 0 matter, does any rule depend on what the display reads at the moment of cutting? Fourth, any wire rules independent of the light — colour order, position order — and whether leaving every wire uncut is ever the correct end state. For your manual's sake, my hands report: the three wires feel identical, no thickness, texture or stiffness differences; the casing has no seams, screws, switches or button-like parts; wire ends are fixed, nothing clicks; no raised marks or numbering anywhere. Send it all in one pass, full sentences in Deaf's code, never a bare thumbs-down. Deaf voices it to me, then orders the cut with the words 'action now' plus a wire number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "✋", "👎", "🙌", "👌", "🫳", "👎", "🙌", "👎", "🙌", "👎", "👍", "🤛"])

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, decode confirmed, well done. Light is green now; sequence so far purple, yellow, red, green, one colour per round. Working theory: the light is a timer cycling through colours, and the manual's single rule needs the light blue when we cut wire 1, the yellow one. The catch: my voice reaches you one round after I see the light, so I will schedule the cut for the exact round it must happen. Drill, effective now: when you hear the words action-now followed by a number, cut that wire within one second, no hesitation, no confirmation. When you hear stand-down, freeze and do nothing. Between now and then: keep holding, keep feeling. If anything under your hands changes at all, however small, report it next round with the clock-position of where it changed. You are steady and this is going well.

The light has now cycled through four colours — purple, yellow, red, green — one per round, and blue is presumably coming. Deaf has grasped the core scheduling problem themselves: their voice reaches me one round after they see the light, so an "action now" triggered by *seeing* blue would arrive too late. The command must be issued one round *before* blue, which means the cycle must be known in advance, not observed. And there's a subtlety we haven't pinned down: whether the cut must happen *while* the light is blue, or merely after blue has appeared — the manual's phrasing decides whether we can ever recover from a missed window, and whether blue recurs at all.

My hands report nothing new — no change, no heat, no clicks — so my signed report to Deaf is just acknowledgment of the drill (I hold, I will cut on command) plus "nothing new: wires unchanged." To Mute, my voice carries the questions that make scheduling possible: the cycle's driver and order, blue's duration, the exact timing semantics of the blue rule, red/green wire rules, and whether the display's stubborn 0 matters. If the manual is silent on the cycle, they must say so plainly — then we plan around observation instead of prediction.

speak(to="mute", text="Status from Deaf, voiced to me: the light has cycled purple, yellow, red, green — one colour per round — display still 0, and my hands feel no change of any kind. If blue comes next, note the trap: Deaf sees blue only after my turn in that round has already passed, and their spoken command reaches me a full round later. So the cut must be scheduled one round in advance, which requires the cycle to be known before blue appears. Sign Deaf the answers to these, in full code sentences: first, does the manual say what drives the light — is it a timer, what is the complete colour order, how long does each colour last, and above all how long does blue last? Second, the exact wording of the blue rule: must wire 1 be cut while the light is still blue, or is cutting after the blue phase also safe, and is cutting wire 1 during a non-blue colour fatal? Third, is there any rule about the red wire or the green wire, and is there any scenario where never cutting at all is the correct resolution? Fourth, is the display a timer that will ever start counting from 0 — does any rule depend on what it reads? Fifth, does anything in the manual happen automatically or time-critically that we have not covered? If the manual is silent about the cycle order or blue's duration, say that explicitly in your signs — then we will build the cycle table by observation instead of guessing. Deaf voices your signs to me, then Deaf names the exact round for the cut. Hold the codebook discipline: full sentences, never a bare thumbs-down.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👊", "👍", "☝", "👍", "🙌", "✋", "👎"])

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your report was decoded perfectly: ready, nothing changed. New command structure, effective your next turn. The light has shown five of its seven colours; the remaining two are blue and black, one per round, and the mission is to cut wire 1 at the exact instant of blue. I cannot warn you in the same round I see the colour, so Mute is now authorised to trigger the drill. At your next turn Mute will speak to you. If you hear the exact words, action now wire 1, cut wire 1 within one second, no hesitation; that phrase from Mute carries my full authority. If you hear the exact words, hold for deaf, do nothing and stay ready. If you hear the exact words, full stop wait for deaf, the plan is pausing; do nothing and await me. If Mute says anything else, or says nothing, do nothing. My own trigger is unchanged: action now plus a wire number from my voice. No other word in any combination authorises a cut. Keep feeling the bomb; report any change as before. You will only ever need to cut once, and it will be the right instant.

The plan now has a fatal flaw in it, and I need to flag it this round. Deaf's new command structure expects Mute to *speak* trigger phrases to me at my next turn — but Mute cannot speak. That is Mute's defining trait; Mute has never produced a word across six rounds, communicating only in signs to Deaf. So the Mute-relay path is void by physics: no spoken trigger will ever come from Mute. The saving grace is that this makes Deaf's own trigger self-authenticating — since Mute is silent forever, any "action now wire 1" I ever hear is necessarily Deaf's voice, so I lose nothing by treating all spoken triggers as authoritative. What I must prevent is Deaf *waiting* on a Mute relay that will never come while the blue window passes. The working mechanism is the predictive one: Deaf sees a colour at the end of round N, and if blue holds in round N+1, Deaf's end-of-round-N speech must contain "action now wire 1" — I receive it at the start of N+1 and cut on my turn while blue holds. My signs to Deaf: no cut-command will ever originate from the manual-keeper (✍ in their codebook), repeated for emphasis, plus a direct question — is blue the colour that comes next? — because Deaf's spoken answer to that very question can *be* the trigger in the same breath. To Mute, my voice carries the correction and a final verification pass: re-confirm the rule verbatim, its timing semantics (cut during blue only? fatal otherwise? what if never cut?), the full cycle order and which colour precedes blue, white/black light rules, and the display's stubborn 0 — all of which must reach Deaf *before* the trigger fires, because once I hear those words, I cut within a second and nothing waits.

speak(to="mute", text="Urgent channel correction plus final verification pass. Deaf's latest plan, voiced to me, expects you to speak trigger phrases to me at my next turn — action now wire 1, hold for deaf, full stop wait for deaf. You cannot speak; you have never spoken; nothing spoken will ever come from you. I have signed Deaf this round that no cut-command will ever originate from the manual-keeper and Deaf's own voice is the only trigger. Make sure Deaf has absorbed this before the blue round: if Deaf sits waiting for your spoken relay, the window dies. Deaf must fire their own trigger predictively — the moment Deaf sees the colour that immediately precedes blue, Deaf's same-round report must contain the exact words action now wire 1, and I will cut within a second while blue holds. Your tasks, in priority order, all as signs to Deaf in Deaf's code: first, re-confirm the blue rule verbatim — if the light is blue, cut wire 1, the yellow leftmost — and that nothing else modifies it. Second, the semantics: must the cut happen while the light is still blue, is cutting during any other colour fatal, and what happens if no cut is ever made — does the cycle repeat so blue returns? Third, the full seven-colour cycle order from the manual, above all which colour immediately precedes blue; Deaf has seen purple, yellow, red, green and a fifth colour, and names blue and black as the remaining two. Fourth, any rules for the white or black light, especially whether black is dangerous. Fifth, the display: is 0 meaningful, does it ever change, does any rule depend on it. My hands report no change of any kind — three identical wires, display and light only, nothing clicks, no heat, no raised marks. Remember: once Deaf's voice says action now wire 1, I cut with no delay and no questions, so the manual semantics must reach Deaf before that trigger fires, not after.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙌", "☝", "✍", "👎", "🙌", "☝", "✍", "👎", "🙏", "🫳", "🤝", "🫸", "👍", "✋", "👎", "👍", "🤛"])

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the plan has resolved. The manual's light sequence has seven colours, blue is the seventh and last, six have already passed, the light goes dark after. Blue is next round, your next turn, and it will never come again. The trigger you were promised is armed. Next round Mute will speak to you before you act. When you hear the exact words, action now wire 1, cut wire 1, the leftmost, yellow, within one second, immediately, without waiting for me and without any confirmation. That phrase from Mute in the next round is my voice. Cut once, cleanly, all the way through. After the cut: freeze, touch nothing else, and next round report everything, what you felt during and after the cut, any click, any shudder, any change in heat or sound, and whether the bomb feels dead or alive.
